newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT-India's statement on new gold import rules.
newsitem.headline: TEXT-India's statement on new gold import rules.

text.p: Following is the text of a statement by the Indian Finance Ministry on the easing of gold import restrictions.

"Passengers of Indian origin or passengers holding valid Indian passports and coming to India after a period of not less than six months of stay abroad are allowed to import gold on a payment of customs duty at the rate of 220 rupees per 10 grams.
However, such passengers can import gold up to a maximum limit of five kg, and they are required to pay customs duty in convertible foreign currency.
Despite this provision of legal imports, smuggling of gold through unofficial channels is taking place in quantities which is still a matter of concern to the government.

During the course of recent discussions in the Consultative Committee of the Parliament attached to the Ministry of Finance, the Members of Parliament were generally of the view that the existing policy of import through baggage route deserves to be liberalised so as to reduce the smuggling of gold through illicit channels.
Similar demand was made by members from different political parties in the Lok Sabha (lower house) while the Finance Minister replied to a question on gold import policy in the Lok Sabha recently.
On careful consideration of the matter, the government has decided to raise the existing limit of five kg to 10 kg.

The enhanced limit of 10 kg up to which gold can be imported by passengers would come into force from 1st January, 1997. There is no change in the rate of customs duty which continues to be 220 rupees per 10 grams."
